title: The Moon Has a Hidden Face. It Looks Nothing Like Ours

scenes.text: The Moon has a hidden face, and it looks nothing like ours.
The same side always points at Earth. Nobody saw the far side until a probe photographed it in 1959.
Our side is about a third dark lava plains. The far side has just one percent. It's a pale world of craters with a crust up to twice as thick.
In 2024, China brought back the first rocks ever collected from the far side. Scientists now think they know why.
Earth's gravity heated the near side more while the young Moon was still molten, so lighter rock drifted to the far side and piled up.
So the face you see every night is the thin, melted, scarred one. Would you rather stand on the side nobody sees?

description:
The far side of the Moon looks nothing like the side we see.
About 31 percent of the near side is dark volcanic plains, but only about 1 percent of the far side is, and its crust is far thicker. In October 2026, researchers studying rocks returned by China's Chang'e-6 mission, the first samples ever collected from the far side, proposed that uneven tidal heating from Earth drove the young Moon's magma ocean to pile lighter rock onto the far side.
Would you rather stand on the side nobody can see from Earth?
